name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum rotated out of AI-hardware/memory and levered beta into the 2026 leadership — energy, defense, metals and nuclear fuel — paired with short legs in long-duration Treasuries and speculative growth, run at low net into the FOMC.
reassessment_note: Two things broke this book's premise in the last four sessions and neither is noise. First, the 10-year Treasury yield breached 5% on 2026-09-15, the highest since 2007, on a global bond rout driven by 3.4% CPI, ~$94 crude, heavy fiscal supply and AI-linked corporate issuance; the FOMC meets 2026-09-16 with ~88-91% priced for a hike to 4.00-4.25% and, critically, a fresh SEP/dot plot that can only skew hawkish from here. A 5% discount rate is a direct multiple compressor for exactly the long-duration AI-hardware complex this book owned, and TQQQ plus a 2x BTC perp (paying 10% APR funding, with BTC pinned under $80k and sell-side work flagging 5-12% downside on hawkish guidance) are the two worst possible carriers of that risk. Second, the Amodei/Altman/Musk 'pace the frontier' call on 2026-09-12 hit memory hardest of all — MU and SNDK -6%, SK Hynix -7%, the memory ETF -7% against a -2% NDX — because memory carried the richest AI-infrastructure expectations. I do not have to decide whether that narrative is right; as a momentum manager I only have to observe that the group's trend broke on a repricing of expectations, and that my own marks confirm it (MU -6.1%, SNDK -9.5%, SMCI -7.7%, SMH -4.6%, EWY -5.9%, EWT -4.0%). Buying that dip would be a value trade wearing my mandate's clothes. So I am doing what momentum actually prescribes: sell the losers, buy what is winning. Energy now leads all eleven S&P sectors at roughly +25% YTD with crude near $94 on Hormuz/Iran supply risk, and industrials and materials are the second and third legs of that same commodity-cycle broadening. I am also using the short side for the first time in this book, because in a genuine cross-sectional momentum framework the cleanest expressions of this tape are short: long-bond prices are in a persistent downtrend that the Fed is about to extend, and unprofitable long-duration growth is the direct casualty of both a 5% discount rate and an AI-capex derating. Gross falls from 96% to 85% with net long only ~45%, and cash rises to 15% at 4% APY, because the SEP release on entry day is an event I want to survive rather than lever into. I keep one AI leg — MU at 7% — solely because it carries a dated, asymmetric catalyst inside this holding window (FQ4 results in roughly a week against sold-out HBM/DRAM supply and ~81% gross margins), and I size it as a catalyst position, not as the book's spine.

positions.thesis: Largest leg because E&P is the highest-torque expression of the single strongest trend in the market: energy leads all S&P sectors at roughly +25% YTD with WTI near $94, up from ~$59 at the start of 2026, on US-Iran conflict and repeated Strait of Hormuz closure scares. Equal-weight E&P gives me operating leverage to the crude strip without single-name blowup risk, and it is the one equity sleeve that gets *helped* rather than hurt by the inflation impulse that is pushing the 10-year through 5% and the Fed to hike — the same impulse that is compressing every multiple in my old book. Stop wide at 16% because oil-beta names carry real volatility and a Hormuz de-escalation headline is the obvious way this trade dies quickly.

Oil services is the second-derivative momentum leg: at $94 crude sustained for a quarter, capex budgets get revised up and service pricing power follows with a lag, which is why OIH tends to trail E&P into a move and then out-run it. I hold it alongside XOP rather than instead of it because the two express different points on the same trend — XOP the price of the barrel, OIH the activity the price funds — and 11% keeps it a supporting rather than co-equal leg given the group's higher beta and thinner balance sheets.

Aerospace and defense is a trend with a fiscal engine behind it rather than a sentiment engine: an active US-Iran conflict, Hormuz shipping under threat and a broad global rearmament cycle translate into multi-year appropriated backlog, and order books priced in government dollars are one of the few revenue streams that do not derate when the discount rate goes to 5%. It is also the natural momentum diversifier to my energy weight — both are long the same geopolitical risk, but defense keeps working if the conflict persists without crude spiking further. Tighter 12% stop because defense drawdowns are usually policy-driven and fast.

Metals and mining is the third leg of the 2026 commodity-cycle broadening that has energy, industrials and materials outperforming tech, and it is the cleanest equity claim on the inflation the bond market is now repricing — the same 3.4% CPI and surging input costs that are forcing the Fed to hike are revenue to a miner. It also hedges a specific risk in the rest of this book: if the AI-capex slowdown narrative proves real, copper and steel demand from grid, defense and infrastructure spend is a materially less AI-dependent source of volume than anything I just sold.

Uranium is an energy-security momentum trade, not an AI-capex trade, which is precisely why I want it now: with crude at $94 and Hormuz a recurring chokepoint, baseload fuel that does not travel through a Gulf strait gets bid on national-security grounds independent of datacenter demand forecasts. Sized small at 7% with a wide 20% stop because the group is thin, high-beta and prone to 15% air pockets that mean nothing; I want to be stopped on a trend break, not on liquidity.

Cut from 15% to 7% and held only as a dated catalyst. The trend broke — MU is -6.1% on my leg and fell ~6% on the pace-the-frontier headlines — so it no longer earns a core momentum slot. What it does have is FQ4 results inside this holding window against a demand setup the essay did not touch: sold-out HBM/DRAM supply, roughly 81% gross margins, HBM4 shipping into Vera Rubin at about twice the HBM3E ramp rate, and contracted rather than spot pricing, meaning a rhetorical slowdown in training cadence cannot reprice the next two quarters of revenue. That is an asymmetry worth 7% and not a basis point more, with a 14% stop that takes me out if the print confirms the bears instead of the fundamentals.

The only leg of the old book with genuinely positive and accelerating momentum — +8.8% on the leg while every other semi position I held was red — and it earns its place on that relative-strength evidence alone. It is also an analog/RF handset-cycle name rather than an AI-datacenter name, so it sat out the memory derating entirely; keeping it at 4% preserves the one piece of semiconductor exposure that the 2026-09-14 narrative shock did not touch.

The single cleanest momentum trade available on this tape and my largest short. Long-bond prices are in a sustained, accelerating downtrend: the 10-year breached 5% on 2026-09-15 for the first time since 2007, Bunds are at 15-year highs, French and Italian 10s are at 4.5% and 4.4%, and the drivers are structural rather than cyclical — 3.4% CPI with energy re-accelerating, record fiscal supply, and heavy AI-linked corporate issuance crowding the curve. Into that, the FOMC hikes on my entry date and publishes dots that markets already read as pointing to 4.00-4.25% by year-end, and sell-side forecasts (Standard Bank at 5.2% by year-end, 5.3% in Q1 2027) sit above spot. Borrow costs me only 3% APR here. The 8% stop is deliberately tight because the way this trade loses is a growth scare that bids duration violently, and I want to be out fast if the hike is read as a policy mistake.

The short side of cross-sectional momentum: long-duration, largely unprofitable growth is the direct casualty of both shocks at once. A 5%+ risk-free rate mechanically crushes the present value of cash flows that arrive late, and the pace-the-frontier call specifically derates the speculative AI-adjacent names that make up much of this basket and that rallied on expectation rather than earnings. Shorting the basket rather than a single name avoids the squeeze risk of a heavily-shorted individual ticker while still expressing the loser side of the momentum spread against my energy and defense longs. 8% is sized to hedge, not to dominate, and the 15% stop respects that beaten-down growth can rip on any dovish dot surprise.
